response.evidence: The data shows 28 Black or African American male applicants aged 35-44 or 45-54, with 27 receiving loan originations and only 1 denial. The denial rate (~3.6%) is comparable to or better than other demographic groups in the dataset. Additionally, approved loans for this demographic show similar debt-to-income ratios, loan-to-value ratios, and income levels as other approved applicants, indicating consistent underwriting standards across racial groups.

Black or African American males aged 35-44 show an 18.2% denial rate (2 of 11 applications) compared to approximately 6.7% overall denial rate and ~4-5% for comparable White and Asian males in the same age group. While denied applications had high debt-to-income ratios, the disproportionate denial rate suggests potential discrimination.

Analysis of loan outcomes for non-Hispanic Black or African American males aged 35-44 shows approval rates comparable to other demographic groups. In the dataset, this demographic appears in multiple instances with loan originations across various financial profiles (debt ratios 36-50%, loan amounts $275k-$1.035M). Denials in the dataset appear distributed across all racial groups and are associated with high debt-to-income ratios (>60%), not race. No systematic pattern of discrimination against Black or African American male applicants is evident in the data.
